result.title: When a Permitted Action Completes a Forbidden Workflow: Designing Consequence-Oriented Approval for LLM Agents
result.comment: Under Review at the 41st AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-27)
result.summary: Tool-using language-model agents increasingly ask people to approve consequential actions, yet an approval prompt shows only the next step. A request to send a file to an approved recipient can look harmless even when that file was assembled, several steps earlier, from data the user said must never leave. We call this a cumulative authorization failure and argue that it is an interaction design problem as much as a security problem. The evidence a reviewer needs is spread across the trajectory, and listing it in time order leaves the reviewer to reconstruct the causal chain. We present the Cumulative Consent Ledger (CCL), an approval interface built on four design principles that restate the user's intent, bind the review to the exact action, compose the cumulative consequence, and keep every claim checkable. A trusted monitor that tracks artifact lineage supplies the evidence. In a between-subjects study with 80 participants and 960 approval decisions, CCL was associated with fewer unsafe approvals than an evidence-matched chronological log (24.2% vs. 32.5%), higher comprehension, and faster decisions, although the adjusted difference in unsafe approvals remained uncertain (-7.9 points, 95% CrI [-19.7, 3.8]). In a system evaluation, the monitor detected 89.2% of 120 violating checkpoints and, used as an execution gate, reduced executed unsafe effects from 43.3% to 5.0% for one agent at a small cost to benign completion. We derive implications for designing consent around consequences rather than individual calls.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出「累积授权失败」：单步动作看似无害，但多步累积后果可能违背用户意图，属于交互设计问题；作者提出 Cumulative Consent Ledger 审批界面（重述意图、绑定具体动作、合成累积后果、保持可核查），配合追踪工件来源的可信监控器，并用 80 人 960 次审批决策的被试间实验及系统评测检验。
AI.relevance_reason: 轨迹级证据的合成与可核查性、以及基于累积状态做审批/放行判断，可能与 LVR 中跨步证据聚合、latent 状态是否保留可核查的任务必要信息及停止决策的评价问题构成概念类比，可供核查。
